explanation: `ParseDuration` replaces `dur` for each nonzero integer or fractional part, so only the last part survives. In `Duration.ParseDuration`, `2h3m4s` produces `d = 4s` instead of the expected `2h3m4s`; fractional inputs such as `1.5s` produce only `500ms` instead of `1.5s`. In `Duration.FormatParseRoundTrip`, parsing `1h0.000000002s` leaves `dur = 2ns` instead of `1h0.000000002s`; negative mixed-unit cases likewise lose earlier parts. Adding each signed integer and fractional contribution preserves the full sequence and combines both parts of a component. The existing default-zero `Duration dur` supplies the initial accumulator value.

edits.old:
if (int_part != 0) dur = sign * int_part * unit;
    if (frac_part != 0) dur = sign * frac_part * unit / frac_scale;
edits.new:
if (int_part != 0) dur += sign * int_part * unit;
    if (frac_part != 0) dur += sign * frac_part * unit / frac_scale;
